'''Nitol Niloy Group''' ({{Langx|bn|নিটল নিলয় গ্রুপ}}) is a [[Bangladeshi]] diversified conglomerate based in Dhaka. Its primary business is the import and distribution of [[Tata Motors]] vehicles in Bangladesh.<ref>{{cite web |title=About Nitol Niloy Group |url=http://www.nitolniloy.com.bd/NNG/About.Aspx |access-date=2 June 2021 |website=nitolniloy.com.bd}}</ref> [[Abdul Matlub Ahmad]] is the chairperson of Nitol Niloy Group.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2012-02-07 |title=Nitol-Niloy Group opens 'export house' |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-221359 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref> [[Selima Ahmad]] is the vice-chairperson of Nitol Niloy Group.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Profile of Selima Ahmad, President, BWCCI |url=http://www.bwcci-bd.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=145&Itemid=121 |access-date=2021-06-02 |website=www.bwcci-bd.org}}</ref>

== History ==
Nitol Niloy Group was established in January 1980 as Nitol Motors Limited, an importer of vehicles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Welcome to Nitol Motors Limited |url=http://www.nitolmotors.com/about |access-date=2021-06-02 |website=www.nitolmotors.com}}</ref>

Nitol Motors Limited became the distributor of Tata Motors in Bangladesh in 1988.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tata Motors - Leading Automobile Manufacturer in Bangladesh |url=https://www.tatamotors.com.bd/about-us/ |access-date=2021-06-02}}</ref>

In 1991, Nitol started assembling trucks and buses for Tata in Bangladesh.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=2018-09-06 |title=Nitol-Niloy to start assembling Tata pickups this month |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news/business/nitol-niloy-start-assembling-tata-pickups-month-1629904 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref>

Niloy Cement Clinkerization started operations in September 2007.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2007-09-10 |title=First-ever cement clinker plant in private sector starts operation |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-3388 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref> It was the first [[cement clinker]]ization plant in Bangladesh.

The group has an annual turnover of 5 billion taka in 2010.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2010-05-16 |title=Nitol-Niloy plans tie-up with Tata on coal power plant |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-138651 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref>

Nitol-Niloy Group led a delegation of Bangladeshi companies to Uganda in May 2011.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=2011-05-23 |title=Bangladesh to get 60,000 hectares for farming in Uganda |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-186836 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref> It announced plans to invest US$12.5 million to develop rice cultivation in Uganda.<ref name=":1" /> It signed an agreement with [[Amrit Group]] to develop a poultry industry in Bangladesh.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2011-03-28 |title=Nitol-Niloy and Amrit sign $10m deal |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-179392 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref> It opened a driving school in [[Kishoreganj District]] called Nitol-Tata Driving Training Institute.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2011-11-23 |title=Nitol-Tata driving school opens today |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-211323 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref>

Nitol Niloy Group controlled [[FAS Finance and Investment]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Sakib |first=Shanaullah |title=88pc loans go to PK Halder's pocket |url=https://en.prothomalo.com/bangladesh/crime-and-law/88pc-loans-go-to-pk-halders-pocket |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=Prothom Alo |language=en}}</ref> It pulled out its investment from FAS Finance and Investment and the company was taken over by [[PK Halder]] who embezzled 13 billion taka funds from the financial institute.<ref name=":2" />

Nitol Niloy Group signed an agreement with Hero MotoCorp to invest US$40 million to establish a motorcycle plant on 20 April 2014.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hero MotoCorp, Nitol Niloy to set up bike plant in BD |url=https://en.prothomalo.com/business/Hero-MotoCorp-Nitol-Niloy-to-set-up-bike-plant-in |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=Prothom Alo |language=en}}</ref>

In 2016, Nitol Niloy Group requested permission from Bangladesh Bank to invest US$7 million in Gambia but were denied permission.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |date=2017-09-19 |title=Akij may get nod to buy Malaysian firms |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/business/akij-may-get-nod-buy-malaysian-firms-1464358 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=BD govt refuses to allow Nitol-Niloy to invest in Gambia |url=https://www.jagonews24.com/en/international/news/23941 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=jagonews24.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Later Finance Minister [[AHM Mustafa Kamal|A. H. M. Mostafa Kamal]], who is in favor of foreign investments by Bangladeshi companies, requested them to submit a detailed investment plan to the central bank which they failed to do.<ref name=":3" />

Nitol Niloy Group announced plans to assemble Tata pickups under Nita Company Limited, a joint venture with Tata Motors, in September 2018.<ref name=":0" /> Production was scheduled to begin in 2020.<ref name=":0" /> The project suffered delays due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2020-07-20 |title=Pandemic puts a damper on Tata pickup project |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/business/news/pandemic-puts-damper-tata-pickup-project-1933205 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref> The company had also expressed an interest in assembling small cars of Tata in Bangladesh.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-09-26 |title=MEDIA-Bangladesh's Nitol Niloy group keen to assemble Tata Motors' small cars - Business Standard |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/media-bangladeshs-nitol-niloy-group-keen-idINL4N1M71JT |access-date=2021-06-02}}</ref> Bangladesh is the fourth largest market for Tata motors.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2012-12-20 |title=Nitol-Niloy launches new commercial vehicle |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-261896 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref> It is also delayed the launch of an electric vehicle assembled in Bangladesh due to the pandemic.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2020-11-10 |title=Nitol's electric car arrival pushed back by pandemic |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/business/news/nitols-electric-car-arrival-pushed-back-pandemic-1992245 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref>

Nitol Niloy Group is part of the Star Infrastructure Development Consortium which has 17 Bangladeshi conglomerates.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |date=2018-08-16 |title=Mega steel plant in the works |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news/business/mega-steel-plant-the-works-1621420 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref> Star Infrastructure Development Consortium plans to open a US$3.5 billion steel plant in Chittagong in partnership with Kunming Iron & Steel Holding Company Limited.<ref name=":4" /> It also has a joint venture with [[Hero MotoCorp|Hero Group]] to produce motorcycles in Bangladesh.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kanungo |first=Soumonty |date=2017-08-28 |title=Bangladesh a perfect market for Tata Nano: Nitol Niloy's Abdul Matlub Ahmad |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/KZba6KjBDq090pwRPai18K/Bangladesh-a-perfect-market-for-Tata-Nano-Nitol-Niloys-Abd.html |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=mint |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2014-07-18 |title=Mega motorbike show in September |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/mega-motorbike-show-in-september-33784 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2019, Nitol Niloy Group received a license from the [[Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority]] to establish [[Kishoreganj Economic Zone]]. The group planned to invest 3 billion taka to develop the 84-acre site.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2019-02-18 |title=Nitol Niloy gets final licence today |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/business/news/nitol-niloy-gets-final-licence-today-1703740 |access-date=2021-06-02 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref>

extract: Nitol Niloy Group (Bengali: নিটল নিলয় গ্রুপ) is a Bangladeshi diversified conglomerate based in Dhaka. Its primary business is the import and distribution of Tata Motors vehicles in Bangladesh. Abdul Matlub Ahmad is the chairperson of Nitol Niloy Group. Selima Ahmad is the vice-chairperson of Nitol Niloy Group.
